claim: Kenneth French's 49 Industry Portfolios dataset assigns each NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stock to one of 49 industry portfolios at the end of June of year t using its four-digit SIC code at that time, then computes returns from July of t to June of t+1, with daily, monthly, and annual return files spanning July 1926 to the present.
limitations: Describes portfolio construction only, not the I-20260923-01 select-window return numbers (those are a local, first-party computation on the downloaded official files); industries are cap-weighted stock baskets, not directly investable, and carry no leverage, so mapping to a specific leveraged sector ETF is an extra step this iteration makes, not something French's page claims.
quote: We assign each NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stock to an industry portfolio at the end of June of year t based on its four-digit SIC code at that time.

claim: Moskowitz and Grinblatt (1999, Journal of Finance) document a strong and prevalent momentum effect in industry components of stock returns that accounts for much of the individual-stock momentum anomaly: industry momentum strategies that buy past winning industries and sell past losing industries are highly profitable even after controlling for size, book-to-market, individual stock momentum, cross-sectional dispersion in mean returns, and microstructure effects, while individual stock momentum is significantly less profitable once industry momentum is controlled for.
limitations: Unlevered, equal- or value-weighted industry portfolios rebalanced monthly with no transaction costs modeled at the ETF-spread level; a decades-old sample that predates our 2023-2026 selection and holdout windows and predates the existence of any of the five candidate leveraged-ETF lanes; does not address leverage, daily reset, or volatility targeting at all.
quote: This paper documents a strong and prevalent momentum effect in industry components of stock returns which accounts for much of the individual stock momentum anomaly.

claim: Hsieh et al. (arXiv 2504.20116) show that leveraged ETF performance depends fundamentally on return autocorrelation and return dynamics rather than only volatility drag: in markets with independent returns LETFs exhibit positive expected compounding on their target multiple, serially correlated (trending) markets enhance daily-rebalanced LETF returns, and mean-reverting regimes cause underperformance.
limitations: Theoretical/simulation paper with an empirical section limited to SPY and QQQ, not to any of the five candidate 2x/3x sector ETFs (NUGT, JNUG, FAS, DPST, DFEN); a preprint, not yet peer reviewed; does not itself claim any specific industry will trend in 2026.
quote: We show that this view is incomplete: LETF performance depends fundamentally on return autocorrelation and return dynamics.

claim: Direxion's DPST (Daily Regional Banks Bull 3X ETF) seeks a return of 300% of its benchmark index for a single day only; the fund should not be expected to provide three times the benchmark's cumulative return for periods greater than a day.
limitations: Marketing/product page, not a prospectus; states the objective and single-day caveat but not the historical magnitude of compounding decay or borrow/financing costs, which are inside the fund NAV and not visible on this page.
quote: This leveraged ETF seeks a return that is 300% of the return of its benchmark index for a single day. The fund should not be expected to provide three times the return of the benchmark’s cumulative return for periods greater than a day.

claim: Direxion's NUGT and DUST (Daily Gold Miners Index Bull and Bear 2X ETFs) seek a return of 200% or -200% of their benchmark index for a single day only; the funds should not be expected to provide two times or negative two times the benchmark's cumulative return for periods greater than a day.
limitations: Marketing/product page; NUGT's own since-inception NAV return is reported as -31.53%, a reminder that a trending-regime lane can still have a negative full-history return outside the regime it trends in, which is why this round scores lanes only on the frozen 2023-2026 windows, not since-inception performance shown on this page.
quote: These leveraged ETFs seek a return that is 200% or -200% of the return of their benchmark index for a single day. The funds should not be expected to provide two times or negative two times the return of the benchmark’s cumulative return for periods greater than a day.
